about: The fields Topgent supplies to the behaviour rules, and where each comes from. A field not listed is unknown to every rule. Changing this file changes rule coverage: regenerate fixtures with scripts/f-fixtures.py.

fields.evt.type: the Audit syscall record; the process sensor for an exec
fields.evt.res: SUCCESS, or the error name from the return value
fields.evt.arg.flags: the open call's flags, as O_* names
fields.evt.arg.oldpath: the Audit PATH records of a rename or link
fields.evt.arg.newpath: the Audit PATH records of a rename or link
fields.evt.arg.target: the target text of a symbolic link
fields.evt.arg.name: the Audit PATH record
fields.evt.arg.filename: the Audit PATH record of an exec
fields.evt.arg.mode: the chmod or mkdir call's mode argument, as S_I* names
fields.evt.arg.request: the ptrace call's request argument, by name
fields.evt.arg.uid: the setuid call's argument, named by the host's account database
fields.evt.arg.cmd: the bpf call's command argument, by name
fields.evt.arg.domain: the socket call's domain argument, as an AF_* name
fields.fd.name: the file a call named, from the Audit PATH record, with . and .. resolved; unknown for sockets, whose local address Audit does not record
fields.fd.nameraw: the file a call named, as the program passed it, placed under the working directory
fields.fd.typechar: f for a file, 4 or 6 for an internet socket, u for a local one
fields.fd.num: the open call's descriptor or -1 when it failed; the socket descriptor of a network call
fields.fd.sip: the peer address of a network call
fields.fd.sport: the peer port of a network call
fields.fd.ip: the peer address of a network call
fields.fd.port: the peer port of a network call
fields.fd.net: the peer address of a network call
fields.fd.snet: the peer address of a network call
fields.fd.rnet: the peer address of a network call
fields.fd.cip: the peer address of an inbound accept or datagram receive
fields.fd.cnet: the peer address of an inbound accept or datagram receive
fields.fd.cip.name: absent unless a future DNS sensor observes a client name; socket metadata itself carries only the address
fields.fd.name_changed: whether a datagram call supplied a peer address for that operation; false for accept, listen and connect
fields.fd.sockfamily: ip or unix, from the address family
fields.fd.l4proto: tcp, udp, icmp or raw, from the socket call that made the socket, which the eBPF source watches; unknown through Audit, which does not record it, and for a socket made before the probe loaded or inherited from a parent
fields.proc.name: the Audit record's process name; the process sensor
fields.proc.exe: the first exec argument, as the program was invoked, from Audit's exec arguments held in memory
fields.proc.exepath: the program path from the Audit record or process history
fields.proc.aname: process history, one ancestor per index or all at once
fields.proc.aexe: process history, one ancestor per index
fields.proc.cmdline: the exec's Audit arguments, held in memory only
fields.proc.args: the exec's Audit arguments, held in memory only
fields.proc.pcmdline: the parent's exec arguments, when Audit saw that exec, in memory only
fields.proc.tty: whether the process has a controlling terminal: Audit records its terminal; the eBPF source follows task_struct.signal->tty through BTF and supplies 0 or 1
fields.proc.cwd: the working directory, ending in /: the Audit record's; on the eBPF source, walked in the kernel for every exec and for a call with a path relative to it, as the process sees it from its own root
fields.proc.duration: the event time less the process start time
fields.proc.vpid: the last NSpid value from /proc/<pid>/status while the process still exists: its pid in the innermost namespace; unknown after it exits
fields.proc.is_vpgid_leader: whether /proc/<pid>/stat reports the process id as its process-group id while the process still exists
fields.proc.is_exe_from_memfd: whether the program path is an anonymous memory file
fields.user.name: the user id, named by the host's account database; in a container, by the container's own /etc/passwd when it can be read (the eBPF source)
fields.user.loginuid: the audit login user id, -1 when unset; the eBPF source reads it from the task when this kernel records it
fields.container.id: host, for a process in the host's pid namespace; the container's short id when the eBPF source named it from the event's own cgroup, else from a running process's /proc/<pid>/cgroup
fields.container.image.repository: absent for a host process; in a container, the image's repository as Docker states it, when Docker can be asked while the container exists (the eBPF source)
fields.container.privileged: absent for a host process; in a container, whether Docker runs it privileged (the eBPF source)
fields.container.mount.dest: absent for a host process; in a container, mount destinations from Docker inspect, matched exactly or by the catalogue's trailing wildcard (the eBPF source)
fields.k8s.ns.name: absent for a host process; in a container, the pod namespace the kubelet's labels give, absent for one no kubelet started (the eBPF source)
fields.k8s.pod.name: absent for a host process; in a container, the pod name the kubelet's labels give, absent for one no kubelet started (the eBPF source)
fields.thread.cap_effective: the caller's effective capability set, as CAP_* names, read from its credentials through BTF (the eBPF source); Audit does not record it
fields.thread.cap_permitted: the caller's permitted capability set, as CAP_* names (the eBPF source); Audit does not record it

sources.about: What each syscall source cannot supply, and whether it names the container an event ran in. Coverage is counted for the source actually delivering: a field one source lacks is unknown on it.

blind_to.Read environment variable from /proc fil: read-only opens under /proc/ are dropped in the kernel, 97% of all opens on a measured host (docs/ebpf/PLAN.md, E4)

host_only.about: Fields Topgent answers the same way for every process in the host's pid namespace: container.id is host, and a host process has no container image, pod or mounts, so the rest are absent. For a process in a container they are what its runtime says, or unknown.
